title: Cymbal and drum makers: Turkish, Zildjian, Ludwig, Slingerland
summary: Moore moved from Turkish cymbals to Zildjians and uses Ludwig drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: By the way, just up to the time you were with Pete Brown and Don Frye with the trio, and a little before that, who were some of the prominent drum-makers and cymbal-makers that you would get your drums from? What companies, that is, were selling the drums that you preferred to use?
During that time, I was using the Turkish cymbal.

Zildjian was kind of expensive. I couldn't get up all that money to get them Zildjians until later on. The Turkish cymbal, which had a nice sound, but it had a loud, harsh sound which was very thick. And there's another cymbal between the Turkish and the Zildjian that had a nice sound. But the Zildjian cymbals were the top cymbals. It's kind of expensive, but it's a good cymbal. I use two of them right now. I use a Zildjian cymbal which is 22-inch, and I have one that's 20-inch. I only use two cymbals. One of them has the rivets in it, to get that surging sound. Of course, for hi-hats, I use 14-inch hi-hat cymbals.
What about the other equipment, like your snare drum...? What were the sets...? Was the Gretsch Company... They were active at that time, weren't they? Gretsch?
Well, there was Gretsch, but they didn't have very much of a name during that time. It's always been an expensive drum, because it's a good drum. But the drum I mostly use is a Ludwig.
Yeah, the Ludwig. And after a while, Ludwig and Slingerland got together. I think Slingerland bought Ludwig out.
Slingerland. Yeah. Is that what happened? I guess that's so.
Ludwig was (?) Slingerland, I think it was. Probably about the same time. But one bought the other one out.
